name: LoMa
plain: LoMa (Nordström, Edstedt et al. 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: DaD keypoints, DeDoDe-G descriptions (VGG19 plus DINOv2) and a light LightGlue-style transformer matcher; matches as keypoint index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). MIT code and weights; DINOv2 Apache-2.0.
summary: LoMa (Nordström, Edstedt et al. 2026): local feature matching with a light transformer. DaD (a VGG11 detector trained by distillation, Edstedt et al. 2025) finds 2048 keypoints per image, the DeDoDe-G descriptor (VGG19 + a frozen DINOv2 ViT-L/14) describes them, and nine LightGlue-style transformer layers (rotary self-attention, cross-attention) refine the descriptions before a dual-softmax assignment. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their scores.
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
No exportable module: the match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
Two resizes per image as upstream: the detector sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.
Upright only: the released weights are not trained for in-plane rotations.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

variants.name: loma-b

training_data.name: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth)

licence.training_note: Matcher: MegaDepth (paper); DaD: MegaDepth-based distillation (DaD paper); DeDoDe-G descriptor: MegaDepth; DINOv2 (frozen): LVD-142M (Meta).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.011 vs the original. GPU, portable bfloat16 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.002 and p99 <= 0.001 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).
